text: HTTPS is the foundation of secure web communication, encrypting data between users and servers to prevent eavesdropping. However, security goes far beyond encryption. Strong authentication, such as multi-factor login, ensures only authorized users access sensitive areas. Equally important is input validation—never trust user data. Without it, attackers can inject malicious code through forms, leading to common vulnerabilities like SQL injection or cross-site scripting. These flaws allow data theft or unauthorized actions. Therefore, developers must sanitize inputs, secure outputs, and regularly update software. A single oversight, such as a weak password policy or unpatched plugin, can compromise an entire website. Staying vigilant and testing for weaknesses are essential practices for every developer.
